questions.prompt: An exterior angle of a triangle is 110° and one opposite interior angle is 45°. Find the other opposite interior angle in degrees.
questions.explain: Exterior angle = sum of the two opposite interior angles: 110 − 45 = 65.

questions.prompt: Which rule proves two right triangles congruent if their hypotenuses and one other side are equal?
Prove that if two lines intersect, the vertically opposite angles are equal.
questions.modelAnswer: Let lines AB and CD meet at O. ∠AOC + ∠AOD = 180° (linear pair on CD). ∠AOD + ∠BOD = 180° (linear pair on AB). So ∠AOC + ∠AOD = ∠AOD + ∠BOD (both equal 180°). Subtracting ∠AOD from both sides, ∠AOC = ∠BOD. Similarly ∠AOD = ∠BOC.
